transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~92 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel, Jonas Rivera, Priya Banerjee, Alex Cho (Redwood); Tara Nguyen, Samir Khatri, Elena Ruiz, Diego Morales, Lina Park (Acme)

Optional sections:
Summary: Cross-functional tabletop to align on traffic ramp, failure modes, severity classification, and who touches what during a canary soak. Focus on data residency, SSO failover, and what constitutes a rollback vs staged degradation.
Topics: canary sizing, soak-test plan, severity matrix, telemetry gaps, security gating, next steps
Action items: see metadata list above

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: All right hi everyone, thanks for joining. I think we should kick off — main goal today is to agree on the severity matrix and the staged traffic plan for the upcoming migration window. We have about an hour and a half.
[00:36] Tara: Sounds good. We'll be mostly listening but also want clarity on who we call at 2am if things pop.
[01:12] Jonas: Hey, quick intro — I'm Jonas, SRE on the Redwood side. I'll be owning canary infra and the immediate mitigation steps. Quick note: we plan to use prefix caching and the KV cache thresholds — apologies my mic's echoing — to avoid tail latencies during the soak.
[01:45] Diego: Can you explain what you mean by KV cache thresholds? We've seen odd evictions cause latency spikes.
[02:10] Alex: Yeah, so the runtime has a KV cache that holds recent token keys, if eviction is too aggressive it adds recomputation overhead. We'll share recommended settings but also want to test with your tenant sequences because Acme's calls are high-context.
[02:46] Samir: Right, our real sequences average 1.2k tokens per request during batch overnight processing, that might stress the cache.
[03:15] Priya: For the soak, we propose a 4-hour window with three stages: 10% production traffic, 40%, then 75% for last hour, then back down. We need to define thresholds that trigger a roll-back vs staged-degradation.
[03:50] Lina: What's the objective at 75%? Is it to validate scale or to validate latency SLOs?
[04:10] Priya: Both. We want to validate throughput, KV hit-rate, and that tail latency stays under the SLO. But if error rate exceeds X or p99 latency doubles, we fall into a severity-two and throttle.
[04:38] Elena: Also, from security, we need to confirm audit log retention and KMS key access is not affected during the canary. If anything changes we want an automatic rollback.
[04:58] Jonas: Understood. We'll ensure KMS access is unchanged and that logs are mirrored to your SIEM. We'll add a fast check pre-soak.
[05:25] Maya: Quick aside — last time we had a mislabeling in the routing policy and a subset of tenants hit a lower-quantized model by mistake. We flagged it as a process gap. We're adding a routing assertion step before ramp.
[05:55] Samir: Can you remind us which quantized model? We saw inference quality skew and some hallucinations in the transcripts.
[06:15] Alex: That was our 8-bit fallback, the model alias got swapped in the routing table — sometimes the export name is 'redwood-dedication' in the logs and that confused our selector, transcription might call it 'dedication' — sorry, misc audio from the last call.
[06:48] Diego: Heh yeah I remember 'redwood-dedication' in the logs.
[07:05] Priya: So in the severity matrix document we will explicitly list: S1 = data loss / PII leakage, S2 = sustained p99 > 3x baseline for 10 minutes or error spike > 5%, S3 = transient latency blips or single-tenant errors. Thoughts?
[07:38] Lena: (sic) — Lina: That seems reasonable, but for Acme we also want a category that captures degraded quality that impacts revenue but not availability. Maybe call that S2b?
[07:58] Maya: We can add S2b for 'quality regression' where we throttle to slower model but keep calls alive.
[08:16] Elena: Any automated switch for S2b? We don't want silent quality changes without notification.
[08:34] Alex: We'll wire alerts for divergence on a small eval set — if the embeddings similarity or intent accuracy dips below a threshold, it fires a quality alert. That can trigger auto-rollback of quantization or model variant.
[09:01] Samir: Important: what's the rollback time we should assume? In previous runbooks we had up to 12 minutes for full model swap.
[09:23] Jonas: Realistically, with our sockets warm, a model variant swap is ~5-8 minutes for gradual traffic shift; if we have to reprovision nodes it's longer. We'll document expected timelines in the runbook.
[09:47] Maya: Okay let's walk through the soak timeline and playbook. Jonas, you take infra; Priya you take communications and product thresholds; Alex you take the validation checks; Maya will coordinate with Acme leads.
[10:15] Jonas: Step one: pre-soak checklist — verify canary size (initial 2 pods with the same GPU profile), ensure autoscaler is disabled for the canary group, confirm KV cache settings set to 'lenient' to reduce churn, and pre-warm KV cache with synthetic prefix workload.
[10:45] Diego: Can you outline what 'lenient' equates to numerically? We need numbers for our own runbook.
[11:02] Jonas: Sure, eviction age 180s, max entries per tenant 120k, soft limit triggers at 75% memory. We'll publish exact values.
[11:26] Priya: Communications: At each stage we need a sync channel. We'll use a dedicated Slack #acme-canary and a pinned status doc. Stage transitions will have a 15-minute holding period for telemetry review.
[11:53] Samir: Who's authorized to progress traffic? We want only two people: Acme on-call and Redwood SRE lead.
[12:12] Maya: Agree. For our side it'll be Jonas or Diego, and for Acme it's Samir or Tara.
[12:30] Elena: About the audit logs — if we detect an unexpected permission change, we want an auto-halt. Is that possible?
[12:46] Alex: We can add a small lambda that watches KMS policy changes and posts a halt signal. It won't be fully automated into the traffic controller yet, but we'll have a human-in-the-loop strong lock until we test it.
[13:10] Priya: Okay next area: observability gaps. We currently don't have token-level cost breakdown per route in the canary dashboard — that matters if cost spikes.
[13:34] Jonas: We can add per-route token counters but it won't be retroactive. We'll add them to the canary dashboard and make a short-term alert for token-cost anomalies.
[13:52] Diego: Also we need higher sampling for debug traces during the soak; please make the default trace rate 10% for canary traffic.
[14:10] Alex: Noted. We'll increase trace sampling and store traces for 48 hours.
[14:28] Maya: Quick question from me — what are our fallbacks if the canary shows a progressive quality regression but infra metrics look fine? Do we pause, rollback, or route to a slower model?
[14:50] Alex: The policy will be: for quality regressions below S2 threshold, we do S2b — route to baseline model variant (not quantized), notify teams, and keep traffic. If quality keeps degrading, then full rollback.
[15:12] Samir: Can you guarantee that routing to baseline doesn't spike latency unacceptably? We need numbers.
[15:30] Jonas: Baseline increased per-token CPU cost, expect 10-20% latency increase; we'll clamp latency by reducing concurrency per pod if needed. We'll add those knobs to the runbook.
[15:55] Priya: Let's capture the communication pattern for incidents: S1 — all-hands, pageing, exec notif; S2 — on-call + product + CSM; S3 — ticket and next-day follow-up.
[16:20] Tara: And we need a clear post-mortem owner for any S2/S1. We'll default to Acme platform lead + Redwood SE for shared ownership.
[16:40] Maya: Good. Now a short dry run scenario: imagine during the 40% stage p99 jumps 2.3x and error rate climbs from 0.2% to 2%. Walk me through who does what.
[17:02] Jonas: First we pause progression, we revert any recent routing changes, pin traffic back to 10%, escalate to SRE runbook, check KV eviction and GPU saturation, then if error persists run a canary rollback.
[17:28] Diego: If it's tenant-specific, we can quarantine that tenant and keep others live.
[17:36] Lina: How do we quarantine? Is that automatic?
[17:44] Alex: We'll run a route exclude for affected tenant ids — one command in the routing controller — it's manual by design. We'll add a script to make it faster.
[18:05] Priya: Telemetry thresholds: we'll set p99 baseline from last 30 days, and set the alert at 2.5x baseline sustained for 5 minutes, or a sustained error spike of 1% absolute over baseline.
[18:30] Elena: One security ask: any data retained in buffers during failed requests must be scrubbed and not stored in logs.
[18:46] Alex: Agreed — we'll ensure error traces redact prompt tokens and do not persist PII.
[19:05] Maya: Good. A few notes about stakeholder comms — we will send out a 24-hour pre-note, a 1-hour pre-note, and then stage transition notes. We'll own the status doc and Jira epic.
[19:30] Samir: On capacity — can we get 2 additional nodes for the canary? Our peak tests last time pegged CPUs.
[19:45] Jonas: Yes I put that in action items — will provision and test them in staging before Friday.
[20:03] Priya: Any other gaps?
[20:20] Diego: We should run a scripted failure injection where we simulate a DB latency of 800ms on one shard to see how the system copes.
[20:40] Alex: We'll schedule that as a separate exercise — mark it as optional for the soak but recommended.
[21:00] Maya: Okay time check — we've covered matrix, soak stages, telemetry, and comms. Quick recap and owners?
[21:18] Priya: I'll publish the severity matrix and a communication plan by Monday (2026-11-15).
[21:30] Jonas: Provision canary nodes and publish KV settings by 2026-11-17.
[21:42] Alex: I'll prepare the validation checks and trace config plus a quick smoke script by 2026-11-14.
[21:55] Maya: I'll consolidate runbook links, send the staged traffic schedule to Acme, and coordinate the pre-soak checks by 2026-11-13.
[22:10] Tara: We'll confirm on our side who does the approvals and add emergency contacts.
[22:25] Lina: One more ask — can you include a small eval set from Acme to track quality? We'll scrub it for PII.
[22:40] Alex: Yes we can do that, but we need the dataset preferably hashed or anonymized.
[22:58] Maya: Great. Anything else?
[23:10] Elena: Nothing else from security, thanks.
[23:20] Diego: No, good call.
[23:30] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll share the doc updates and follow up with calendar invites for the soak window and the post-mortem slot.
[23:45] End meeting.
